speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with weakness and fatigue; to begin my assessment, have you noticed if these symptoms worsen with physical activity or if you have experienced shortness of breath? Also, have you had any recent weight changes or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 33-year-old woman. The patient reports feeling extremely fatigued and weak, especially towards the end of the day, to the point of difficulty in self-care. She mentions experiencing these symptoms currently. The patient has been traveling, hiking, and camping recently and notes having had multiple illnesses in the recent past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history, Mrs. Agent. Given your recent hiking, camping, and multiple illnesses, could you describe the specific nature of those recent illnesses, and do you have any history of tick bites or outdoor insect exposure? Please also tell me if you have noticed any muscle weakness in specific limbs or difficulty climbing stairs.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness and fatigue. I also have Mild diplopia.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The presence of diplopia (double vision) alongside fluctuating weakness and fatigue, despite a history of outdoor activities which might suggest Lyme disease, points strongly toward an autoimmune neuromuscular junction disorder. Given the diagnostic criteria and the specific symptom of diplopia, I am confident in this diagnosis.
